name: TN-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+17 district with incumbent Tim Burchett seeking re-election
Burchett's dominant fundraising edge: $2.4M raised and $967K on hand versus $398K for Barnett
Prediction markets price the Democratic win chance at only about 4%
No public polling, no expert ratings, and no outside spending on either side
model.rationale: The seat's deep Republican lean, Burchett's incumbency, and his roughly six-to-one fundraising advantage leave Barnett without a visible path, and markets agree at about a ninety-five percent Republican chance. With no polls or outside money signaling trouble, a double-digit Republican margin is the clear expectation.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Burchett or any polling showing him below the mid-fifties would be the first sign the race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Tim Burchett, the Republican incumbent, seeks another term in a Knoxville-area district that leans roughly seventeen points toward the GOP. He holds a large financial edge, having raised about $2.4 million and kept nearly $970,000 on hand, while Democratic challenger Michaela Barnett has raised about $398,000 with limited cash remaining. No outside groups have invested in the race on either side.

Public polling is absent, and rating organizations have not listed the contest, so the assessment rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing. Prediction markets give Burchett roughly a ninety-five percent chance of winning. Barnett's fundraising shows some local engagement, but nothing in the available evidence points to a competitive race; the expectation is a comfortable double-digit Republican win.
